evidence_quotes:
Level should be within 1/2 in.
(12.7 mm) of fill plug opening when vehicle
is on level ground.

Differential level should be
within 1/4 inch (6.4 mm) of fill plug
opening when lubricant is cold or to plug
level when hot.
statements.reason: The transfer-case level is within 1/2 inch; the cold differential level is within 1/4 inch.
statements.statement: The permitted distance below the fill opening is the same for a transfer case on level ground and a differential with cold lubricant.

evidence_quotes:
Level should be within 1/2 in.
(12.7 mm) of fill plug opening when vehicle
is on level ground.

Differential level should be
within 1/4 inch (6.4 mm) of fill plug
opening when lubricant is cold or to plug
level when hot.
statements.reason: The supplied maintenance table gives a fluid-level specification for each of those operating conditions.
statements.statement: The standard fluid-level specification accounts for both a transfer case on level ground and a differential with cold lubricant.

statements.reason: The cited conditions have different limits—1/2 inch and 1/4 inch—and the supplied passages do not establish the proposed range regardless of condition.
statements.statement: For a transfer case on level ground and a differential with cold lubricant, the fluid level should be within the manufacturer's specified range, typically 1/2 inch to 1 inch below the fill opening; the answer says this range applies regardless of ground conditions or lubricant temperature.

statements.reason: The supplied passages contain fluid-level guidance but do not identify that manual or volume.
statements.statement: TM 9-2320-280-20-1, Volume 1 contains detailed fluid-level guidelines.
